sections.html:
Happy Valley is a suburban city in the northwest corner of Clackamas County, about 13 miles southeast of downtown Portland. It covers roughly 12 square miles and borders Portland, Clackamas, Sunnyside and the area that used to be the City of Damascus.

The land rises toward Mount Scott, an extinct volcano in the Boring Lava Field that tops out near 1,050 feet. Scouters Mountain and Mount Talbert are the other high points locals mention, and the city zones large parts of them as open space.

sections.h2: How did Happy Valley start, and why did it incorporate?
sections.html:
Happy Valley began with the Deardorff family, who claimed 640 acres under the Donation Land Claim Act of 1850, and it incorporated on August 25, 1965.

The 1965 vote passed 111 to 66 at the fire station on King Road, making it the eleventh city in Clackamas County. Residents acted because Portland was expanding south and annexing nearby land, and a new state law taking effect that August would have blocked incorporation within three miles of an existing city. About 300 people lived here then. The first mayor, James Robnett, was chosen by coin toss after a tied council vote.

The name itself is folklore. The city's history page says it may come from local boys who sang loudly after drinking cider near Sunnyside church, or from an early sales pitch aimed at future land buyers.

sections.h2: How fast has Happy Valley grown?
sections.html:
Happy Valley grew from 4,519 residents in 2000 to an estimated 28,916 in 2025, more than six times larger in 25 years.

Much of the housing here dates from that run. In the 2020 census, 78.5 percent of occupied housing was owner-occupied, 44.2 percent of households had children under 18, and the 2023 American Community Survey put median household income at $120,324.

After voters dissolved the City of Damascus in May 2016, more than 1,000 acres, mostly in the western part of the old city, were voluntarily annexed into Happy Valley.

Annexation matters to sellers because it changes the tax bill. The city says its own rate is $0.67 per $1,000 of assessed value. Compared with staying in urban unincorporated Clackamas County, annexation adds roughly $1.34 per $1,000, and for the former Damascus area it adds roughly $2.04. On a $370,000 assessed value, the city's examples work out to about $495 and $755 a year. The city adds that annexing owners get around-the-clock police coverage, four code enforcement officers and city public works services, and there is no annexation fee.

Check whether your parcel sits inside city limits or still in the county before you price the house. A buyer will ask, and the answer shifts the yearly cost of ownership. The Clackamas County Assessment and Taxation office can confirm exact numbers.

sections.h2: What is the Pleasant Valley and North Carver area?
sections.html:
Pleasant Valley and North Carver is a planning area of about 2,700 acres east and south of Happy Valley's existing neighborhoods, set up for future homes and jobs.

The city's plan covers roads, parks, schools, sewer and water together. Sewer planning falls to Clackamas County Water Environment Services, and Sunrise Water Authority handles the water side. Schools in the plan area include North Clackamas School District, Centennial and Gresham-Barlow, and North Clackamas voters approved a bond for more classrooms and a new high school.

New subdivisions in this part of the city will compete for the same buyers as resale homes elsewhere in town, so sellers should look at what is under construction near them.

Services are growing with the population. The city has run the Happy Valley Library since July 2015 at 13793 SE Sieben Park Way, and it broke ground in 2023 on an expansion of more than 10,000 square feet. Amenities like that tend to come up in buyer conversations, so mention them when you describe the neighborhood.

sections.h2: What building rules does Happy Valley enforce?
sections.html:
Happy Valley follows a development code with a required architectural look for commercial and mixed-use buildings, which the city calls the Happy Valley Style, a modern Cascadia design drawing on craftsman, prairie and rustic styles.

  • The city adopted a comprehensive plan before the Metro urban growth boundary was drawn in 1978.
  • A single zoning map ties land use to the plan, so a lot can only be used in ways that map allows.
  • Developers must often build or upgrade water and sewer lines, roads, trails and parks at their own cost.
  • Open space such as Scouters Mountain and Mount Talbert Nature Parks stays protected.

Master-planned neighborhoods named in the city's materials include Taralon, Jackson Hills and The Reserve. If your house sits in one, ask your title company early about any homeowners association dues and transfer fees, since those rules vary by community.

sections.h2: How do roads and schools work for a Happy Valley house?
sections.html:
Sunnyside Road is the commercial spine named in the city's design materials, and the Highway 212 corridor just east of town is one of the state's busiest east-west freight routes.

Clackamas County led a Sunrise Corridor Community Vision Plan with ODOT, Metro and the city, accepted in 2025 and now in its implementation phase. It covers safer streets, walking and biking links, green space and river access east of the city. Most of the city is in the North Clackamas School District, which Wikipedia reports as running two high schools, two middle schools and eight elementary schools here.

Rain adds one more factor. The area averages about 48 inches a year, which is high for the Portland region. Roofs, gutters and drainage deserve a look before any buyer inspection.

sections.h2: What do property tax dates look like for a Happy Valley owner?
sections.html:
Happy Valley owners pay Clackamas County property taxes in three parts, due November 15, February 15 and May 15. In 2025 the first date shifted to November 17 because the 15th fell on a Saturday.

A full payment by the first date earned a 3 percent discount in 2025, and two-thirds earned 2 percent. The county reported 170,621 statements that year and an average single-family real market value of $691,382 countywide, with an average taxable value of about 54 percent of that. Those are countywide figures, not Happy Valley figures. Appeals to the Property Value Appeals Board were accepted through December 31, 2025.

Read the county's 2025 property tax announcement for the full schedule, and ask your closing agent how the current year will be split between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: What do Happy Valley sellers tend to run into?
sections.html:
Sellers in Happy Valley mostly deal with a handful of situations, and each affects the timeline.

  • Annexation questions: buyers want to know which tax rate applies.
  • Newer construction nearby: fresh builds set the standard buyers expect.
  • Slopes and rain: hillside lots can need drainage or retaining work after a wet year.
  • Community rules: master-planned neighborhoods can carry association dues and resale paperwork.

A cash sale skips the buyer's loan approval and lets you choose a closing date that fits a move or an estate timeline. Ask for the terms in writing, compare them to the costs of prep and listing, and decide from there.

faqs.q: What county is Happy Valley, Oregon in?
faqs.a: Happy Valley is in Clackamas County, about 13 miles southeast of downtown Portland. Property tax bills and recording go through Clackamas County.

faqs.q: When did Happy Valley become a city?
faqs.a: Residents voted to incorporate on August 25, 1965, by a margin of 111 to 66. About 300 people lived in the community at the time.

faqs.q: How many people live in Happy Valley?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 28,916 residents as of July 1, 2025. The city counted 23,733 in the 2020 census and 13,903 in 2010.

faqs.q: Does annexation raise property taxes in Happy Valley?
faqs.a: Yes, according to the city. It estimates about $1.34 more per $1,000 of assessed value for urban unincorporated Clackamas County and about $2.04 more for the former Damascus area, with the city's own rate at $0.67 per $1,000. Confirm exact numbers with Clackamas County.

faqs.q: When are Clackamas County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payments are due November 15, February 15 and May 15, with the next business day counting if a date falls on a weekend. A full payment by the first date earns a 3 percent discount.
